subject: general
question: A river 20 m deep and 36 m wide is flowing at the rate of 2.7 km/hr. The amount of water (in m³) that runs into the sea per minute is _____.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert speed to **m/min**: 2.7 km/hr × (1000/60) = 45 m/min.

**Volume per minute** = Area of cross-section × Speed in m/min.

Volume = (20 × 36) × 45 = 720 × 45 = 32,400 m³.

**∴ The correct answer is 32,400 m³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Depth** (h) = 20 m, **Width** (b) = 36 m, **Speed** = 2.7 km/hr.

**Formula Used:** Volume of water per unit time = Area × Velocity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f98061d68e3d2a2b49b8c7d16a8a6f5382d683b4f526efee468b68a8e18cfcf8.png] 

⇒ **Speed of flow** in m/hr = 2.7 × 1000 = 2700 m/hr.

⇒ **Speed of flow** per minute = 2700 ÷ 60 = 45 m/min.

⇒ **Cross-sectional area** of river = Depth × Width = 20 × 36 = 720 m².

⇒ **Volume of water** per minute = Area × Length of water column in 1 min.

⇒ Volume = 720 × 45 = 32,400 m³.

**∴ The correct answer is 32,400 m³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Flow Rate Measurement

The volume of water flowing through a channel is calculated as the product of the **cross-sectional area** (Area = Width × Depth) and the **flow velocity** (Speed).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/min, multiply by 1000/60 or 50/3. To convert m³ to Liters, remember 1 m³ = 1000 Liters.

Volume of a Cuboid

Since the river is treated as a rectangular channel, the volume is V = l × b × h, where 'l' is the distance water travels in the given time.</p
